knowledge:
- key_parameters: value_transformation=Specifies how to transform the value column (always the 7th column) to establish a ranking where high values indicate high significance. Use "log_additive_inverse" (i.e., -log(x)) for p-values, Q-values, or FDRs where lower values are more significant. Use "log" for scores where higher values are already more significant.
- alternatives: The original 1D IDR method (Li et al. 2011) which is restricted to 1D genomic data like ChIP-seq peaks. The IDR2D web interface (https://idr2d.mit.edu) which offers similar functionality online.
- when_to_use: Use when measuring reproducibility between replicate genomic experiments. Use estimate_idr2d for 2D genomic interaction data (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Hi-C) and estimate_idr1d for 1D genomic peak data (ChIP-seq).
- pitfalls: Choosing the wrong value_transformation. The ranking is established by sorting the value column in descending order. If the input values are FDRs or p-values (where lower is more significant), failing to use "log_additive_inverse" will result in incorrect ranking and invalid IDR estimation.

workflows.name: two_dimensional_idr
workflows.intent: Identify reproducible genomic interactions between two replicates of 2D genomic data (e.g., ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Hi-C).
input: rep1_df (data frame of replicate 1 genomic interactions with anchors and significance values)
rep2_df (data frame of replicate 2 genomic interactions with anchors and significance values)
workflows.stages: 1. Load replicate data frames ;; 2. Estimate 2D IDR using estimate_idr2d ;; 3. Summarize results using summary ;; 4. Visualize IDR distribution and dependencies using draw_idr_distribution_histogram, draw_rank_idr_scatterplot, and draw_value_idr_scatterplot
workflows.code:
rep1_df <- idr2d:::chiapet$rep1_df
rep2_df <- idr2d:::chiapet$rep2_df
library(idr2d)
idr_results <- estimate_idr2d(rep1_df, rep2_df,
                              value_transformation = "log_additive_inverse")
rep1_idr_df <- idr_results$rep1_df
summary(idr_results)
draw_idr_distribution_histogram(rep1_idr_df)
draw_rank_idr_scatterplot(rep1_idr_df)
draw_value_idr_scatterplot(rep1_idr_df)

workflows.name: one_dimensional_idr
workflows.intent: Identify reproducible genomic peaks between two replicates of 1D genomic data (e.g., ChIP-seq).
input: rep1_df (data frame of replicate 1 genomic peaks with coordinates and significance values)
rep2_df (data frame of replicate 2 genomic peaks with coordinates and significance values)
workflows.stages: 1. Load replicate data frames ;; 2. Estimate 1D IDR using estimate_idr1d ;; 3. Summarize results using summary ;; 4. Visualize IDR distribution and dependencies using draw_idr_distribution_histogram, draw_rank_idr_scatterplot, and draw_value_idr_scatterplot
workflows.code:
rep1_df <- idr2d:::chipseq$rep1_df
rep2_df <- idr2d:::chipseq$rep2_df
library(idr2d)
idr_results <- estimate_idr1d(rep1_df, rep2_df, 
                              value_transformation = "log")
rep1_idr_df <- idr_results$rep1_df
summary(idr_results)
draw_idr_distribution_histogram(rep1_idr_df)
draw_rank_idr_scatterplot(rep1_idr_df)
draw_value_idr_scatterplot(rep1_idr_df)
